solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mushroom producers article fails dismally

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a show that bombs flops badly

explanation.surface: A grower's report: the item meant to raise mushrooms has been a total flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mushroom' is not the fungus here but the cloud left by a nuclear blast.
explanation.definitionFit: Atomic weapons throw up the familiar mushroom-shaped cloud when detonated, so they produce mushrooms.

clue.text: Steer around old Scottish river vessel

indicators.note: the word for steer wraps itself round the other pieces

parts.note: to con a ship is to steer it
auld is Scots for old

explanation.surface: Someone steers a boat round an old river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A large metal cooking pot, the witches' kind, is a vessel for boiling.

clue.text: Resistance encountered after Free Scots shot novelist

indicators.note: encountered after means the resistance letter comes after the jumbled Free Scots
shot means wrecked or ruined, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A resistance fighter meets the Free Scots and a novelist is shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' rearranges the nine letters of 'Free Scots' into CSFORESTE: the author's two initials and the first part of his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: C. S. Forester was the English writer of the Hornblower naval novels.

clue.text: Optimistic expectation for catching fish, given decent information

indicators.note: the word for holds the other pieces as if catching them

parts.note: an eel is a fish
decent means good
a fact is a piece of information

explanation.surface: An angler hopes for a catch, given good tips on where the fish are.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a general sense of wellbeing and confidence, such as economists say lifts consumer spending.

clue.text: Food store, being very low, reportedly delivers

parts.note: deep means far down, very low

indicators.note: reportedly means the next word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to deliver someone is to free them

explanation.surface: A food store, sitting very low, is said to make deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: A freezer chest keeps food frozen, a store for it.

clue.text: Love, then husband flees this regretful lady

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the husband leaves, so his letter is taken out of the word this

explanation.surface: A love affair ends as the husband walks out on this sorry woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The lady is from Cole Porter's song Miss Otis Regrets, in which she cannot come to lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Cole Porter's song has its heroine send her regrets, so she is a regretful lady.

clue.text: Writer like Self to change position, renouncing drug

parts.note: as means like
I is oneself, the self

indicators.note: renouncing means giving up, so the drug's letter is dropped

parts.note: to move is to change position
E is ecstasy

explanation.surface: A writer in the mould of Will Self switches sides after giving up drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Self looks like the novelist Will Self, but it is simply I.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Asimov wrote science fiction, including the Foundation and robot stories.

clue.text: Copies produced from photograph on course

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a print is a photograph
a run is a course

explanation.surface: Copies are made from a photo taken on a golf or race course.
explanation.definitionFit: The number of copies made in one go at the press is the edition's batch.

clue.text: Club about to give female support

parts.note: a brassie is an old wooden golf club, a two-wood
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A club is about to give backing to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The undergarment supports a woman's bust.

clue.text: Stunner posed again facing backwards

indicators.note: facing backwards means the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a sitter who posed again resat

explanation.surface: A beauty poses once more, this time turned away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stunner' suggests a beauty, but it is the stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: The electric weapon stuns its target, so it is literally a stunner.

clue.text: Plant originally found on isle brought into factory

indicators.note: the picked letters are put inside the word for factory

parts.note: a mill is a factory

indicators.note: originally means taking the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A plant first found on an island is taken to a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarrow and the water plants of that name are feathery-leaved plants.

clue.text: One delivering mail — not spam for a change

indicators.note: for a change means the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A letter carrier is pleased that, for once, the post is not junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The worker who brings letters to the door is the mail carrier.

clue.text: Beginning to surveille Irish gentleman's address

indicators.note: beginning to means taking the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Starting to watch an Irish gentleman's home address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' looks like a home, but it is a form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is how one addresses a man politely or a knight.

clue.text: Always stocks a good beer, ordered by a keen customer

indicators.note: stocks means holds, so the word for always contains the rest

parts.note: ever means always

indicators.note: ordered means arranged anew, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub that always keeps a good beer is ordered from by an eager regular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' turns BEER into ERBE; 'by' merely sets the second A beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names an enthusiastic, hardworking person, a keen type.

clue.text: See 4
Shield lets axe in once he's reeling

indicators.note: lets ... in means the jumbled letters take the word for axe inside them
together with lets, the word in says one piece goes into another
reeling means spinning drunkenly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to axe is to cut

explanation.surface: A shield admits an axe blow once the man is staggering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reeling' rearranges the letters of 'once he's' into ESCHEON, and 'lets ... in' is split round 'axe', its two halves bracketing the piece taken in.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry this is the shield bearing a coat of arms.

clue.text: Opinion given one way or another

definitions.meaning: a principle held to be true, a belief

indicators.note: a word that reads the same forwards and backwards, whichever way it is given

explanation.surface: A view offered one way or the other.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half describes the word itself: it is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A principle or belief held true is an opinion, and the word is a palindrome.

clue.text: Miserable leak trade pro fixed

indicators.note: fixed means repaired and reset, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wretched leak that a professional tradesman has repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leak' suggests plumbing; it is an eye shedding a tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tear shed in sadness is a drop leaking from an unhappy eye.

clue.text: Raw rock from Who revelatory

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow, spanning both

explanation.surface: Raw rock music from the band The Who proves a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raw rock' sounds like music by The Who, but it is unrefined rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprocessed rock from which metal is extracted is mined mineral.

clue.text: First murderer strangling bishop in hut

indicators.note: strangling means the bishop's letter is held in the middle

parts.note: Cain killed Abel, the first murder in the Bible
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: The first murderer throttles a bishop in a hut.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rough dwelling, such as a log one, is a hut.

clue.text: Lower in sky now, initially rare astronomical sight

parts.note: blue is the sky, as in out of the blue
a lower is a cow, one that lows, and a cow says moo

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the word now

explanation.surface: Something sinking in the sky right now is, at first, a rare sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lower' is read as one that lows, a cow, rather than lower down.
explanation.definitionFit: A second full moon in one calendar month happens seldom, hence once in a blue moon.

clue.text: Post belongings, not seeing the end result

parts.note: post means after, as in post-war

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for belongings is dropped

parts.note: one's effects are one's belongings

explanation.surface: Mailing one's belongings without seeing the final outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A consequence felt later is a delayed result.

clue.text: Two-seater Manhattan Democrat uses

indicators.note: uses means the words employ the letters within them, which are hidden there

explanation.surface: A Democrat in Manhattan gets about on a two-seater.
explanation.definitionFit: A bicycle built for two riders is a two-seater.

clue.text: Good times! Money invested in FT compilers

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so the money goes into the other word

parts.note: the setters of the FT crossword would call themselves us
P, a penny, is a small sum of money

explanation.surface: Boom times: cash is poured into the Financial Times puzzle setters.
explanation.definitionFit: Highs, as in ups and downs, are good times.

clue.text: Crime novelist speaks about medical drama

indicators.note: about means the word for speaks goes round the other piece

parts.note: speaks means says
ER is the American hospital television drama

explanation.surface: A crime writer talks about a hospital TV series.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey detective novels.

clue.text: Forceful police seizing loads to be returned

indicators.note: to be returned means the whole thing is read backwards
seizing means holding, so the police letters go round the other word

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British detective police
loads means many

explanation.surface: Vigorous police seize loads of goods that must be given back.
explanation.definitionFit: Energetic and full of force is the sense of vigorous here.

clue.text: Racing driver appears in three seconds

parts.note: the three seconds are three words for a second, and the first is mo, a moment
the other two are each S, the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A racing driver turns up within three seconds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three seconds' gives three short words for a second: MO, S and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirling Moss was a celebrated British Formula One driver.

clue.text: Old country house secured in 24 hours

indicators.note: secured in means held inside the word for 24 hours

parts.note: a day lasts 24 hours
a house is a home

explanation.surface: An old country house was bought within a day.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African kingdom became today's Benin, so it is a former country.

clue.text: Remove fine fellow attending party

indicators.note: attending means being beside, so the two letters sit next to the party

parts.note: a do is a party
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A fine fellow at a party is told to take something off.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off a hat is to remove it, a gesture of respect.

clue.text: Workers put in very large signs

indicators.note: put in means the workers go inside the size label

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize
men are workers, hands

explanation.surface: Labourers erect some enormous signs.
explanation.definitionFit: Portents of what is to come are signs.

clue.text: Blue perhaps: certainly not in the pink

definitions.meaning: a blue joke is risque, slightly indecent
in the pink means in good health, so this means unwell

explanation.surface: A colour that is blue, but definitely not pink.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both slightly smutty, as a blue joke is, and a little unwell.
